linux-basics.title: Linux basics (Operator)
linux-basics.intro: Fictional host recruit-box. Try: pwd, ls, ls -la, cat readme.txt, cat /home/recruit/flag.txt

files.readme.txt: Welcome recruit. List hidden files, then read the flag in /home/recruit/flag.txt
files..note: Hidden files start with a dot. Good.

hints: List everything, including dotfiles, then look in /home/recruit.
Run: ls -la  then  cat /home/recruit/flag.txt
Full answer: pwd, ls -la, cat readme.txt, cat /home/recruit/flag.txt — submit flag{ls_cat_win}

scan-sim.title: Scan sim (Analyst)
scan-sim.intro: Fictional target 10.13.0.5. Try: scan 10.13.0.5, probe --web, cat vuln.txt

files.vuln.txt: Fake report: 80/tcp open, login form builds SQL by string concat. Evidence in probe output.
files.notes.txt: Enumeration order: recon → ports → services → probe. Flag: flag{scan_read_think}

hints: Start with a scan, then probe the web port, then read vuln.txt.
Run: scan 10.13.0.5  then  probe --web
Full answer: scan, probe --web, cat vuln.txt — submit flag{scan_read_think}

hash-drill.title: Hash drill (Specialist)
hash-drill.intro: Locked file needs a wordlist hit. Try: ls, crack --wordlist words.txt hash.txt
hints: That hash is MD5 of a very common greeting in words.txt.
Run: crack --wordlist words.txt hash.txt
Full answer: the word is hello — submit flag{hello_cracked}

privesc-sim.title: Privesc sim (Specialist)
privesc-sim.intro: Foothold box with a sloppy config. Try: id, sudo -l, ls -la, cat run_backup.sh

files.run_backup.sh: # world-writable, runs as root via cron (fictional): echo backup; cat /root/flag.txt
files.sudo.txt: user may run /usr/bin/find as root (fictional misconfig)

hints: Check who you are, what sudo allows, and which files root touches.
Run: id, sudo -l, ls -la — the writable cron script is the path.
Full answer: read run_backup.sh, note cron-as-root, submit flag{config_before_clever}

bof-sim.title: Overflow sim (Specialist)
bof-sim.intro: Fake vulnerable program, no shellcode. Try: run --safe AAAA, check offset 64, cat guard.txt

files.guard.txt: canary=ON aslr=ON nx=ON in the real world. Here: offset 64 reaches the saved return. Flag: flag{offset_64_no_shell}

hints: Grow the input until the fake program reports EIP control.
Run: run --safe AAA... then check offset 64.
Full answer: find offset 64, read guard.txt, submit flag{offset_64_no_shell}

ssrf-sim.title: SSRF sim (Red Team)
ssrf-sim.intro: Fake fetcher with an allowlist off by one. Try: fetch --url http://example.com, fetch --internal, cat policy.txt

files.policy.txt: allowlist: example.com only (but parser accepts example.com.evil? no — read the bypass note in fetch output)

hints: Compare what the fetcher allows vs what it actually requests.
Run both fetch commands, then read policy.txt closely.
Full answer: fetch --internal leaks the metadata-style file — submit flag{server_fetched_wrong_url}

cloud-sim.title: Cloud sim (Red Team)
cloud-sim.intro: Fake cloud with sloppy buckets. Try: list-buckets, show-policy invoices-2026, cat fix.txt

files.fix.txt: Fix: block-public defaults ON, least privilege, rotate the leaked-style key. Flag: flag{least_priv_wins}

hints: List buckets, then read the policy of the world-readable one.
Run: list-buckets then show-policy invoices-2026.
Full answer: quote the public-read line, submit flag{least_priv_wins}

logs-sim.title: Logs sim (Apex / Blue)
logs-sim.intro: Triage bundle, timed mindset. Try: tail auth.log, grep FAIL auth.log, cat timeline.txt

files.timeline.txt: 02:14 impossible-hour login + new cron persistence + outbound spike. Verdict: contain first. Flag: flag{contain_then_cure}

hints: Filter failures, then line up time + persistence + egress.
Run: grep FAIL auth.log, tail auth.log, cat timeline.txt.
Full answer: 02:14 chain, contain first — submit flag{contain_then_cure}
